Through: Mr.A.S.Khurana, Advoca
 petitioners.

versus
 State (Gnct Of Delhi) And Anr.

Through: Mr.Amit Sahni, APP for  with SI Loveleen, 
 R2/complainant in   CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE YOGESH KHANNA  ORDER % 22.03.2023 1.

Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.636/2016 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Hari Nagar, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 20.12.2015 according to Sikh rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
No child was born from this wedlock.

However, due to matrimonial discord, the couple started living separately from each other since 24.01.2016 and on the complaint of respondent No.2 aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.
During the pendency of proceedings, the couple settled the matter per settlement agreement dated 21.02.2023 before Mediation Centre, Dwarka Courts, Delhi.
The parties have also obtained divorce by mutual consent.

Pursuant to settlement, the petitioner No.1 agreed to pay Rs.18.00 Lacs to respondent No.2 towards all her claims of alimony, maintenance - past, present and future, stridhan, and dowry articles etc.
3.

Out of said sum, the petitioner No.1 has already paid Rs.10.00 Lacs to respondent No.2 and for the balance amount, the petitioner No.1 has handed over draft No.980457 dated 14.03.2023 drawn on Punjab National Bank for Rs.8.00 Lacs in favour of respondent No.2, which has been accepted by her.

4. The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners having left with no claim against them and she has no Jaspreet Singh & Ors vs State (Gnct Of Delhi) And Anr on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44788082/
1 objection if the FIR is quashed.

entities.text: Jaspreet Singh & Ors vs State (Gnct Of Delhi) And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

5. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has received the settled amount from the petitioners.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
6. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.636/2016 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Hari Nagar, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
